mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market softening, which compresses wage growth and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and monthly changes in the S&P 500 over the prior 12 months predicts continued positive momentum in equity returns over the next 20 trading days, provided the correlation remains above 0.6.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when the lagged correlation exceeds 0.6.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals a labor market shock, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS falls by more than 1% month-over-month and UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
